title: Gideon
lead: The fearful farmer from Manasseh whom the angel of the LORD called "mighty fighter," who tested God with a fleece, routed Midian with three hundred men, refused to be king, and then made an ephod that became a snare. His son Abimelech made himself king at Shechem and died by a woman's millstone.

sections.b: The Gideon cycle (Judges 6–8) is the longest judge story before Samson, and its sequel about his son Abimelech (Judges 9) is the Bible's first story of a king in Israel. "The day of Midian" became a byword for a rescue God works with few against many (Isaiah 9:4; Isaiah 10:26; Psalm 83:9–11). Samuel names Jerubbaal among the deliverers (1 Samuel 12:11), and 2 Samuel 11:21 remembers that a woman dropped a millstone on Abimelech. Hebrews 11:32 lists Gideon first among those it has no time to describe. In modern use, "putting out a fleece" means asking God for a sign before a decision, a practice many teachers both Jewish and Christian warn against.
